client_requirement: A real graphical Minecraft Java Edition 26.1.2 client must execute this scenario through the repo-native Gradle runClient adapter (:fabric-agent:runClientAgent, net.neoforged.moddev). That client carries the repo's JVM client-agent bridge for observation and input only and deliberately does NOT load the Solaris Loader mod, so every /trade answer arrives over the ordinary play protocol; it is a no-Loader development client, not an uninstrumented production binary. Protocol bots, wire probes and mock clients do not satisfy this gate.

automation_runner.client_isolation: The primary Gradle runClient uses a per-run game directory and the fixed offline username SolarisPrimary.

scenarios.title: External WASM inventory/storage trade terminal in a no-Loader graphical client
steps: Start Solaris from a fresh world with runtime = "wasm", strict = true, expected = ["inventory-compat"], and explicit storage/inventory_storage_transactions grants. The package declares player_commands = ["trade"], events = ["player.joined", "player.left"], and config.toml mode = "inventory-storage". The trade-ledger key must start absent.
Launch the real graphical 26.1.2 client through the repo-native Gradle runClient adapter (no Solaris Loader mod) and let the agent driver connect it to the loopback server address.

Seed the fixture with explicit operator commands: gamemode survival, /give minecraft:emerald 4, /give minecraft:diamond_pickaxe 1. These are declared debug setup (no_debug_commands = false) and are never claimed as no-debug survival.

Make the seeded tool genuinely component-bearing through ordinary gameplay: /summon minecraft:pig beside the player, select the pickaxe in the hotbar, and land one real survival attack, then require a non-zero client-visible damage component on the pickaxe entry.
Buy twice with /trade buy and require the fresh marker P3_TRADE buy committed ledger=1 then ledger=2 with emerald/apple counts 2/1 then 0/2.
Submit /trade buy a third time with zero emeralds and require P3_TRADE buy refused ledger=2 with byte-identical client inventory (the insufficient-inventory adversarial check).
Submit /trade refund and require P3_TRADE refund committed ledger=1 with emerald/apple counts 2/1.
Submit /trade retry-original while the funds are present and require P3_TRADE retry-original refused ledger=1 with unchanged inventory (the stale storage precondition adversarial check).
Disconnect and rejoin the same player, require the server's session release, then require the persisted emerald/apple counts and the identical damage-bearing pickaxe entry.
Submit /trade stale-session after the rejoin and require P3_TRADE stale-session refused ledger=1 with unchanged inventory (the stale player-session adversarial check).

Capture the inventory after setup, second purchase, refund, rejoin and stale-session refusal. Then probe an ordinary purchase on the new live session: it must still commit with ledger=2 and emerald/apple counts 0/2; capture that final inventory too.
expected_observations: Every /trade submission produces exactly one fresh P3_TRADE marker line in client chat and the driver never accepts a marker that was already visible before that submission.
The committed buys and refund change exactly the client-visible emerald/apple counts the marker claims, and every refusal leaves the whole client-visible inventory unchanged.

The unaffected component-bearing pickaxe keeps its item_id, count, name, damage, max_damage, foil and enchantment list across every phase, across the disconnect/rejoin, and after the stale-session refusal.
The disconnected and rejoined player is the same username, inventory counts persist across the session change, and the stale-session refusal is observed on the new session.
After refusing the old session, the current session still completes an ordinary purchase; a known refusal must not disable the guest or fence unrelated valid work.

No storage revision, refusal reason beyond committed/refused, or durable operation-id receipt is observable from the real client; those gaps are recorded in the scenario report instead of being inferred.
